The authors identify a critical flaw in applying standard Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) to multi-population scenarios: the variance of the estimator explodes as the diversity of the training LLMs increases. Their proposed solution, MMD-MP, is elegantly simple—excluding the intra-class MGT similarity term from the training objective—which theoretically reduces variance and empirically yields a more stable and transferable kernel.

The evidence provided is robust. The authors do not merely claim success; they demonstrate it across a wide array of datasets, LLM families (ChatGPT, GPT2 variants, GPT3, Neo, etc.), and detection tasks (paragraph-level and sentence-level). The theoretical grounding is also solid, with clear propositions and theorems supporting the asymptotic behavior of the new statistic. The ablation studies and synthetic data experiments (Section 5.1) help isolate the causal mechanism of the variance reduction.

In scientific writing, asserting such a fundamental equivalence between training and testing metrics without data to back it up is a notable shortcoming. The lack of one specific experiment validating a claim does not invalidate the entire methodology, but it prevents the paper from being flawless.
